title: Changer+ Launches Stablecoin-First Self-Custodial Wallet to Make Stablecoins Easier to Use
summary: Singapore, Singapore, 6th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Singapore, Singapore, 6th October 2026, Chainwire

Singapore, Singapore, October 6th, 2026, Chainwire

Multi-chain stablecoin wallet combines simpler transfers, flexible gas-fee options, security features, and practical use cases with one ambition: to become the world’s easiest stablecoin wallet.

Changer+ today announced the launch of its self-custodial stablecoin wallet, built to make holding, moving and using stablecoins simpler.

Changer+ supports major stablecoins including USDT and USDC across Ethereum, TRON, BNB Chain and Solana, with more networks and stablecoins planned.

To celebrate its launch, Changer+ is offering new users three free transactions per device on each chain – Ethereum, Solana, and BNB Chain from October 6 to November 6, 2026.

Changer+ is built around a simple belief: people should not need to understand every blockchain, gas token, or transaction mechanic just to use the stablecoins they already have.

Stablecoins Should Just Work

Using stablecoins can still mean figuring out which network a token is on, choosing the right transfer route, sourcing a separate gas token, and navigating unfamiliar transaction steps. Changer+ is designed to move more of that complexity into the background.

“People should not have to become blockchain experts just to use stablecoins,” said Leon Gao, CEO of Changer+, with over a decade of experience in product development in the fintech and payment industry 

“The technology underneath can stay sophisticated. What users see should feel simple, clear and dependable.”

Simplicity Without Giving Up Control

Making stablecoins easier to use should not mean taking control away from the user.

Changer+ is self-custodial, meaning users retain control of their private keys and authorize their own transactions.

For Yun Han Wong, CGO of Changer+, who has spent years working in Web3, preserving that principle is fundamental to trust.

“Trust is everything in Web3,” Yun Han said. “The early crypto idea of ‘being your own bank’ was really about ownership — having control over your own assets instead of simply handing that control to another intermediary.”

“We want to preserve that ethos while making stablecoins much easier to use. Convenience should not mean giving up control.”

Technology and Security Built around the User

Changer+ is designed to remove common friction from everyday stablecoin use.

On supported transactions, Changer+ lets users cover network-related transaction costs without first having to acquire the blockchain’s native gas token. 

For example, a user holding stablecoins does not necessarily need to separately acquire ETH, TRX, BNB, or SOL before completing a supported transaction. 

Changer+ has also completed an independent security audit, vulnerability assessment, and penetration testing (VAPT) conducted by Echo Pulse, a CREST-accredited and Singapore-licensed cybersecurity service provider. 

These capabilities are led by Zack Chen, CTO of Changer+, an NUS-trained technopreneur with years of software development experience overseeing Changer+’s multi-chain architecture and security development.

“Good engineering should reduce the complexity users have to manage while keeping the experience clear and reliable,” Zack said.

Making Stablecoins More Useful

Changer+ goes beyond holding and transferring stablecoins by giving users more ways to put them to practical use.

Current capabilities include global eSIM data plans, a lifestyle ticket marketplace, and security risk signals that help users identify suspicious activity and potentially unsafe addresses, with more use cases planned.

“Our ambition is not to build another wallet people download and forget,” Leon said. “We want to make the whole stablecoin experience easier — from holding and transferring to actually using them.”

As stablecoins increasingly move beyond crypto trading into payments, remittances and everyday digital commerce, the experience of using them remains fragmented across networks and wallets. 

Changer+ was built to close that usability gap. 

Backed by a private family office, Changer+ is taking a long-term approach to building the product. Rather than centering the platform around a project token or speculative rewards, the company is focused on usability, self-custody, security, and practical stablecoin utility. 

“Stablecoins should just work,” Yun Han added. “Fewer unnecessary crypto steps, more useful things you can do with them, and the user stays in control.”

Changer+ is available on iOS and Android.

Download Android app：https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=plus.changer.app&hl=en

Learn more: www.changer.plus

Join communities: https://linktr.ee/ChangerPlus

Contact: [email protected]

Launch Special

Enjoy three free transactions on each chain – Ethereum, Solana, and BNB Chain from October 6 to November 6, 2026.*

Available only to new users who install the Changer+ app and register during the campaign period. Network fees are covered for three eligible transactions per device. Terms and conditions apply. Changer+ reserves the right to amend or withdraw the offer.

About Changer+

Changer+ is a Singapore-incorporated, self-custodial stablecoin wallet built to make stablecoins easier to use.

With multi-chain stablecoin support across major blockchain networks, including Ethereum, Solana, BNB Chain and TRON, Changer+ brings together simpler transfers, flexible gas-fee options, security risk signals and practical use cases — while users remain in control of their private keys.

Backed by a private family office, Changer+ combines payments experience, Web3 expertise and security-led engineering with one ambition: to become the world’s easiest stablecoin wallet.

title: Trump Names Jay Clayton to Lead America’s Super Intelligence Force
summary: Federal efforts to coordinate artificial intelligence (AI) policy will fall to a new Super Intelligence Force, President Donald Trump announced. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton joins three other officials tasked with maintaining U.S. leadership and protecting Americans. Jay Clayton and...
content:
Federal efforts to coordinate artificial intelligence (AI) policy will fall to a new Super Intelligence Force, President Donald Trump announced. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton joins three other officials tasked with maintaining U.S. leadership and protecting Americans.

Key Takeaways

  • The force will engage consumers, religious groups, and AI companies.
  • Clayton says the group has 120 days to assess risks and opportunities.
  • An executive order establishes “Super Intelligence” as the federal government’s preferred AI terminology.

Jay Clayton and Three Officials Lead Federal AI Coordination

Consumers, public interest groups, and technology companies will engage with a new federal task force announced Oct. 4. President Donald Trump named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton among its four leaders when announcing the formation of the Super Intelligence Force on his social media platform Truth Social. The group follows a White House executive order establishing new federal terminology for artificial intelligence.

The president described a mission combining American technological leadership with protection of the public’s interests through coordinated government engagement. He said the effort would “ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence” and “will protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans.”

The other leaders are Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson; Emil Michael, undersecretary of war for research and engineering and chief technology officer; and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor. Engagement also extends to religious organizations and critical infrastructure providers, including operators of essential services. The group reports to the president and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles.

Clayton told The Wall Street Journal that the group has 120 days to assess the technology’s risks and opportunities and determine Washington’s responsibilities. That deadline concerns its findings, separate from the terminology order’s 60-day requirement.

Clayton’s SEC Tenure Includes the Ripple Lawsuit

Clayton’s background includes leadership of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the regulator overseeing securities markets and investor protection. In April 2025, he was selected to serve as interim U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York, before taking his current intelligence role.

The agency sued Ripple Labs and two executives on Dec. 22, 2020, one day before his departure as chairman. Its complaint alleged they raised more than $1.3 billion through unregistered investment contracts involving XRP. Both sides dismissed their appeals on Aug. 7, 2025, leaving a $125,035,150 civil penalty and a court order against future securities registration violations in effect.

The president has linked international competitiveness with American adoption of cryptocurrency and other digital assets, alongside his support for advanced computing. His broader technology agenda has framed both sectors as areas where U.S. leadership depends on encouraging innovation while keeping development and investment centered in the United States.

On July 6, he warned China would take the crypto lead if the U.S. stepped back, comparing the competitive stakes in digital assets with those surrounding other emerging technologies. The remarks reinforced his argument that technological leadership has become part of a wider contest over economic influence and the direction of future industries.

The Trump administration’s federal AI policy framework, released March 20, addressed child safeguards, data centers’ electricity costs, creators’ intellectual property, and worker retraining. The proposals sought national legislation and a uniform approach across the United States.

White House Order Establishes Super Intelligence Framework

A Sept. 29 White House executive order replaced federal AI terminology with “Super Intelligence” and “SI” in official communications and other nonstatutory documents, where permitted by law. It uses the existing legal definition of artificial intelligence and directs the White House science adviser to propose legislative language for a federal definition within 60 days.

The order frames the initiative around maintaining U.S. technological leadership as increasingly capable AI systems develop. It also directs federal agencies to incorporate the new terminology into relevant communications and policy materials where legally permitted.

The administration’s terminology change places the Super Intelligence Force within a broader federal effort to coordinate policy around advanced AI while emphasizing U.S. leadership in the technology.

title: Crypto Licensing Enters a New Era as Global Regulations Accelerate in 2026
summary:
The global digital asset industry is entering a defining chapter as governments and financial regulators continue to introduce comprehensive frameworks for crypto licensing. After years of uncertainty, many jurisdictions are
The post Crypto Licensing Enters a New Era as Global Regulations Accelerate...
content:
The global digital asset industry is entering a defining chapter as governments and financial regulators continue to introduce comprehensive frameworks for crypto licensing. After years of uncertainty, many jurisdictions are shifting away from fragmented oversight toward structured authorization systems designed to improve transparency, strengthen consumer protection, and support sustainable market growth.

Throughout 2026, crypto licensing has become one of the most discussed topics among blockchain companies, fintech startups, institutional investors, and compliance professionals. Rather than treating regulation as a barrier, an increasing number of businesses now view licensing as a competitive advantage that enables international expansion and builds long-term trust with customers.

  • Regulation Is Moving from Guidance to Enforcement
  • Europe Continues to Set the Pace
  • More Jurisdictions Compete to Attract Digital Asset Businesses
  • Institutional Investors Prefer Licensed Platforms
  • Compliance Technology Is Becoming Essential
  • Licensing Influences Customer Trust
  • Challenges Remain for Smaller Businesses
  • The Future of Crypto Licensing

Regulation Is Moving from Guidance to Enforcement

The regulatory landscape has changed dramatically over the past few years. Authorities that once relied primarily on general financial legislation are now introducing dedicated licensing regimes specifically designed for digital asset service providers.

This transition reflects the growing maturity of the industry. As crypto-related services become integrated into payment systems, investment platforms, and digital commerce, regulators are demanding higher operational standards from companies that manage customer assets or facilitate digital transactions.

Businesses entering the market today are expected to demonstrate more than innovative technology. Licensing applications increasingly require detailed governance structures, risk management policies, cybersecurity frameworks, anti-money laundering procedures, and ongoing compliance programs.

The result is a more professional ecosystem where licensed companies are better positioned to attract institutional partnerships and operate across multiple jurisdictions.

Europe Continues to Set the Pace

Europe remains one of the most influential regions in shaping the future of crypto licensing.

The implementation of harmonized regulatory standards across European markets is encouraging companies to rethink their licensing strategies. Instead of maintaining separate compliance approaches for different countries, many organizations are preparing for broader operational frameworks that allow them to serve multiple markets under consistent regulatory expectations.

This shift has created significant demand for legal advisors, compliance specialists, technology providers, and licensing consultants capable of guiding businesses through increasingly sophisticated authorization processes.

Industry experts note that obtaining a license is no longer viewed as the final objective. Maintaining ongoing compliance has become equally important, requiring regular reporting, internal audits, employee training, and continuous monitoring of regulatory updates.

More Jurisdictions Compete to Attract Digital Asset Businesses

While Europe remains a major regulatory hub, competition among international jurisdictions continues to intensify.

Countries across Asia, the Middle East, North America, and offshore financial centers are refining their licensing frameworks to attract responsible digital asset businesses while maintaining high compliance standards.

Many regulators are balancing two important objectives:

  • Encouraging innovation within financial technology.
  • Preventing financial crime and protecting consumers.

This balance has resulted in licensing models that differ in complexity, capital requirements, reporting obligations, and supervisory expectations.

For businesses planning international expansion, selecting the right licensing jurisdiction has become a strategic business decision rather than simply a legal requirement.

Institutional Investors Prefer Licensed Platforms

One of the strongest trends observed during 2026 is the growing preference of institutional investors for licensed crypto businesses.

Banks, venture capital firms, payment providers, and financial institutions increasingly evaluate regulatory status before establishing commercial relationships with crypto companies.

A recognized license demonstrates that a business has undergone regulatory scrutiny and operates within defined legal standards. Although licensing does not eliminate operational risk, it significantly improves credibility and provides additional confidence to partners and customers alike.

This trend is encouraging even early-stage blockchain startups to prioritize licensing much earlier in their development cycle than was common just a few years ago.

Compliance Technology Is Becoming Essential

As regulatory obligations become more sophisticated, technology is playing an increasingly important role in helping licensed companies remain compliant.

Modern compliance solutions now automate many previously manual processes, including customer verification, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, suspicious activity detection, document management, and regulatory reporting.

Artificial intelligence is also beginning to assist compliance teams by identifying unusual transaction patterns, improving fraud detection, and reducing false-positive alerts.

These technological improvements allow licensed businesses to manage growing regulatory responsibilities more efficiently while maintaining operational scalability.

Licensing Influences Customer Trust

Consumer expectations have also evolved considerably.

Retail and institutional users alike are paying closer attention to whether a platform operates under regulatory supervision before depositing funds or using digital asset services.

Market participants increasingly associate licensing with transparency, accountability, and stronger operational controls.

Although no regulatory framework can completely eliminate business risk, licensed providers generally offer greater visibility regarding governance, complaint handling, compliance practices, and customer protection mechanisms.

For many businesses, displaying licensing credentials has become an important component of their overall brand strategy.

Challenges Remain for Smaller Businesses

Despite the positive momentum, obtaining a crypto license continues to present significant challenges, particularly for startups and smaller technology companies.

Application procedures often require extensive documentation, experienced compliance personnel, legal expertise, and ongoing financial commitments.

In addition to initial licensing costs, companies must prepare for continuous regulatory supervision, periodic reporting, independent audits, and evolving compliance obligations.

These requirements may increase operational expenses, but many industry observers argue that stronger regulation ultimately contributes to a healthier and more sustainable market by discouraging fraudulent operators and encouraging responsible business practices.

The Future of Crypto Licensing

Looking ahead, industry analysts expect crypto licensing to become even more interconnected across international markets.

Greater cooperation between financial regulators may simplify cross-border supervision while improving information sharing related to financial crime prevention and consumer protection.

Emerging technologies such as tokenized financial instruments, decentralized finance integrations, stablecoin ecosystems, and blockchain-based payment infrastructures are also expected to influence future licensing requirements.

Rather than slowing innovation, modern regulatory frameworks are increasingly being designed to support responsible growth while maintaining market integrity.

Companies that invest early in governance, compliance, and licensing are likely to benefit from stronger business relationships, improved customer confidence, and greater access to international opportunities.

Crypto licensing is no longer viewed as a niche regulatory requirement reserved for large financial institutions. It has become a central pillar of the digital asset industry and an essential element of long-term business strategy.

As governments continue refining regulatory frameworks throughout 2026, licensed businesses are expected to enjoy greater credibility, stronger institutional partnerships, and improved opportunities for global expansion.

For companies operating in the rapidly evolving blockchain economy, compliance is increasingly becoming more than a legal obligation; it is a foundation for sustainable growth, investor confidence, and long-term success.

title: US Regulators Push National Crypto Rules as America Chases Global Lead
summary: Federal crypto initiatives are advancing across trading, asset custody, and tokenized stocks as Washington pursues global digital asset leadership. The CFTC’s new consultation joins SEC measures aimed at keeping innovation domestic while protecting customers and investors. Two Federal Paths Target T...
content:
Federal crypto initiatives are advancing across trading, asset custody, and tokenized stocks as Washington pursues global digital asset leadership. The CFTC’s new consultation joins SEC measures aimed at keeping innovation domestic while protecting customers and investors.

Key Takeaways

  • SEC relief already covers qualifying tokenized stock trading venues.
  • CFTC plans contemplate reserve verification and customer fund safeguards.
  • Separate SEC custody changes would permit self-custody in certain cases.

Two Federal Paths Target Trading and Crypto Custody

Retail crypto traders could gain tailored protections under a federal initiative launched Oct. 5. The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the regulator of financial contracts tied to underlying assets, opened consultation on a national framework for retail crypto commodity transactions. The effort runs alongside U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) measures addressing asset safekeeping and blockchain-based stock trading.

CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig linked the effort to President Donald Trump’s directive for federal crypto oversight. He said: “I want to underscore that this is a federal option for crypto asset exchanges.”

Preparations for crypto market rules under existing authority began before today’s notice. The proposed crypto asset market category would be a specialized registration option for exchanges offering covered retail trades involving leverage, margin, or financing. These arrangements increase exposure through borrowed funds or collateral. Selig clarified that requiring every crypto exchange to register federally would need congressional action.

Atkins Signals More Rules as SEC Advances Custody Changes

SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins signaled further action in an Oct. 1 statement. The head of the federal securities regulator indicated more crypto regulatory proposals are coming. He argued that outdated requirements should not force onchain markets, where transactions occur on blockchains, offshore.

His remarks accompanied proposed changes to how registered investment advisers and regulated funds safeguard investor assets. The tailored custody framework would permit self-custody in certain circumstances and allow state trust companies as custodians. It also covers adviser audits and broker-dealer safekeeping services for funds.

The Sept. 17 Innovation Exemption already provides temporary, conditional relief for qualifying trading venues and liquidity providers handling tokenized stocks, shares represented on a blockchain. Access restricted to approved participants and equivalent shareholder rights are among its conditions. Federal anti-fraud and anti-manipulation provisions remain applicable.

August’s Regulation Crypto Assets would provide a one-time exemption for certain investment contract offerings of up to $5 million over four years, plus a separate route of up to $75 million per 12-month period. Investment contracts generally involve expected profits dependent on others’ efforts. Both routes would require disclosures; the larger would also demand financial statements and ongoing reporting.

Customer Assets Face Reserve Checks and Direct Delivery Options

Customer protections would build on the Commodity Exchange Act, the federal law governing certain financed retail trades discussed in the agencies’ joint staff statement. Selig’s Oct. 5 remarks outlined proof of reserves, demonstrating assets held for pooled customer property, alongside registered intermediaries handling accounts under disclosure, capital, and segregation requirements, keeping customer property separate from the firm’s own.

Selig also proposes clarifying that transfer to an external noncustodial wallet within 28 days generally satisfies an exception to registered-exchange trading requirements. This follows the withdrawal of earlier digital asset delivery guidance in December 2025. A noncustodial wallet gives its user control over the credentials needed to move cryptocurrencies and other digital holdings.

That distinction concerns the delivery of cryptocurrencies and blockchain-based assets rather than the SEC’s separate proposed custody requirements for advisers and funds. The advance notice of proposed rulemaking gathers preliminary feedback before potential regulations.

Written comments are due within 60 days of publication in the Federal Register, the government’s official publication for regulatory notices. Submissions will be posted on Regulations.gov.

title: Chinese crime network laundered over $1B for Lazarus: ZachXBT
summary: ZachXBT says he infiltrated the network by posing as a customer, gaining information that helped trace funds from the $1.5 billion Bybit hack.
content:
A Chinese organized crime syndicate laundered more than $1 billion stolen in multiple crypto exploits for North Korea’s Lazarus Group, according to blockchain investigator ZachXBT. 

In an Oct. 5 thread on X, pseudonymous blockchain investigator ZachXBT said he posed as a paying client to infiltrate the money laundering network in February 2025, just days after the Bybit hack. He put up $349,700 in stablecoins and took a 5% loss on each order to build trust with one of the network’s operators, known as “Jimmy Green.”

ZachXBT said the operations spanned Hong Kong and mainland China, and information supplied by the launderer helped him identify a cluster of more than $12 million in Bybit-linked funds, with Tether later freezing $442,000 in associated USDt (USDT). 

The investigation offers rare insight into the alleged intermediaries handling North Korea’s stolen crypto. Hackers linked to the country have stolen at least $6.75 billion in digital assets through 2025, according to Chainalysis. 

How North Korea moves stolen crypto

North Korean hackers are known to use a multi-stage laundering process. One method involves chain-hopping and token swapping through decentralized exchanges, bridges and other services to obscure the flow of funds.

Related: SlowMist traces Bitget hack activity to Aug. 31 zero-day exploit

Chinese intermediaries have emerged as an important link in that process. In 2020, US prosecutors charged two Chinese nationals with laundering more than $100 million stolen by North Korean hackers from a cryptocurrency exchange in 2018. 

Source: ZachXBT

In 2023, the US Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned two crypto traders, one from Hong Kong and the other from China, for their role in helping the DPRK convert stolen crypto and bypass financial controls. 

Chinese actors allegedly laundering Bitget funds

ZachXBT has also linked Chinese actors to the laundering of funds from the $387.5 million Bitget exploit in September. 

In a post to X on Sept. 28, ZachXBT said Chinese actors allegedly laundering funds on behalf of the North Korean hackers had been openly seeking support in public Discord servers and Telegram channels operated by services they used. ZachXBT said one of the operators had also been involved in laundering funds from the $292 million Kelp DAO exploit in April.

title: Ripple Targets Turkey’s $200 Billion Crypto Market Amid Lira Pressure
summary: Turkey’s large crypto market is creating opportunities for bank custody and dollar-backed stablecoins, according to Ripple. The company ties its local strategy to currency pressure and evolving regulations as institutions follow consumers into digital assets. Turkey’s $200 Billion Market Meets Evolv...
content:
Turkey’s large crypto market is creating opportunities for bank custody and dollar-backed stablecoins, according to Ripple. The company ties its local strategy to currency pressure and evolving regulations as institutions follow consumers into digital assets.

Key Takeaways

  • Turkey recorded nearly $200 billion in annual transactions, according to Chainalysis.
  • Garanti BBVA’s digital asset service is available to its entire customer base.
  • RLUSD distribution includes Turkish platforms BiLira and Bitlo.

Turkey’s $200 Billion Market Meets Evolving Banking Rules

Turkish consumers and businesses are gaining access to crypto storage and dollar-backed tokens through banking and exchange partnerships, Ripple outlined Oct. 5. The company highlighted its custody and stablecoin operations in Turkey through Garanti BBVA and domestic trading platforms. The latter distribute Ripple USD (RLUSD), its dollar-backed stablecoin, as institutions develop services alongside established retail demand.

Reece Merrick, Ripple’s managing director for the Middle East and Africa, stated:

“We’re seeing genuine demand for regulated, dollar-backed liquidity, and that’s why stablecoins like RLUSD matter here in a very practical way.”

Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis placed Turkey’s annual transaction volume at nearly $200 billion in an analysis published Oct. 23, 2025, with cumulative inflows of approximately $878 billion from early 2021 through mid-2025. Its findings also pointed to growing speculative altcoin trading, involving cryptocurrencies other than bitcoin, alongside attempts to preserve purchasing power amid inflation and lira depreciation.

Turkey’s regulatory framework has developed alongside these services, bringing providers under Capital Markets Board oversight through legislation effective July 2, 2024. Rules effective March 13, 2025, established operating and capital requirements alongside anti-money laundering obligations. According to the Oct. 5 assessment, new safekeeping requirements took effect in June, while transition deadlines remain subject to adjustment as authorized custodians extend their services.

Garanti BBVA Brings Digital Asset Storage to All Customers

Garanti BBVA Kripto, Turkish bank Garanti BBVA’s digital asset subsidiary, combines Ripple Custody with technology company IBM’s infrastructure to protect customer assets. BBVA confirmed the Ripple and IBM partnership in October 2024, following a successful 2023 pilot. The bank subsequently extended the service to its entire customer base. The system safeguards private keys, which control access to holdings, using encryption and other security controls.

The relationship continued into this year, with Merrick describing an extension of Garanti BBVA’s storage partnership in a Jan. 22 post on X. Supported currencies include bitcoin, ether, the cryptocurrency of the Ethereum network, and XRP, the native token of XRP Ledger. Customers can store, transfer, and convert these holdings to or from conventional money.

The company’s latest assessment also emphasizes institutional requirements as banks build services under the country’s licensing regime. It claims to be the only infrastructure provider meeting the regulator’s standards for institutional custodians, framing compliance and operational safeguards as central to its local approach.

Dollar-Backed Tokens Widen Access Through Local Exchanges

Domestic exchange partnerships give Turkish institutions another route to dollar-denominated instruments as currency pressure supports demand for alternatives. The company announced availability through BiLira, Bitexen, and Bitlo on June 2, with that Turkish distribution forming part of its broader expansion. Its Oct. 5 assessment specifically highlighted listings on BiLira and Bitlo.

These tokens are designed to track an external reference value, commonly the dollar, through a mechanism known as a peg. Such stablecoins use reserves and redemption arrangements to support their target price. Their dollar denomination offers an alternative to holding local currency, while reserve quality and the ability to exchange them for cash affect holder risks.

The protections behind these products depend on their issuer’s regulatory structure and the requirements attached to its license. The company detailed the stablecoin’s supervision and reserve framework in September, identifying subsidiary Standard Custody & Trust Company as the issuer under New York Department of Financial Services oversight. The arrangement includes segregated reserves and recurring independent attestations examining backing disclosures.

title: Peter Brandt Hints at Bullish XRP Pattern With a Coffee Cup Chart
summary: XRP’s recent price recovery may be forming a bullish chart pattern, judging from a coffee cup image Peter Brandt placed beneath the cryptocurrency’s trading history. His latest post hints at a possible setup awaiting a breakout. A Coffee Cup Puts XRP’s Gain in Focus XRP investors have a possible bul...
content:
XRP’s recent price recovery may be forming a bullish chart pattern, judging from a coffee cup image Peter Brandt placed beneath the cryptocurrency’s trading history. His latest post hints at a possible setup awaiting a breakout.

Key Takeaways

  • Brandt’s daily XRP chart marks a horizontal level at $1.6572.
  • Reaching the marked level from $1.5230 would require an 8.8% rise.
  • His earlier $5.40 projection came from a separate monthly chart.

A Coffee Cup Puts XRP’s Gain in Focus

XRP investors have a possible bullish formation to assess after veteran trader Peter Brandt shared a daily price chart on X on Oct. 5. The founder of Factor Trading, a proprietary trading and market research firm, placed a coffee cup beneath the token’s recent trading history, suggesting a potential cup-and-handle interpretation of its recovery and subsequent pullback.

The image shows a sharp August advance, a retreat through mid-September, and a recovery toward a horizontal line labeled $1.6572. Recent bars cluster below that line, with the displayed price at $1.5230. Moving from that reading to the marked level would require an increase of approximately 8.8%, placing the potential resistance test above the latest consolidation.

Brandt’s visual shorthand fits his long-standing use of classical chart patterns to evaluate price movements across financial markets. He entered commodity trading in 1976 and founded Factor Trading in 1980. His approach examines recurring structures in historical prices rather than treating enthusiasm for a cryptocurrency as sufficient evidence of an investment opportunity.

What Would Confirm a Cup-and-Handle Pattern?

A cup-and-handle formation generally combines a rounded price recovery with a smaller pullback near the upper part of that recovery. The rounded portion resembles a cup, while the shorter consolidation forms the handle. In Brandt’s image, the coffee cup suggests that interpretation, while the horizontal line identifies a price level above the recent bars.

The distinction between a developing formation and a completed pattern depends on what happens when price challenges its upper boundary. Fidelity describes cup-and-handle confirmation as a breakout above both sides of the cup. Its technical analysis presentation also notes that prices often return toward the breakout area afterward, a movement known as a throwback.

Different chart intervals can reveal different structures, even when they track the same asset over overlapping periods of trading. Candlesticks, resistance levels, and time frames help describe those distinctions. The daily view in the Oct. 5 image emphasizes recent price behavior, whereas a monthly chart compresses years of trading into a longer-term perspective.

Brandt’s Earlier XRP Forecast Adds a Longer View

The latest image follows Brandt’s separate long-term XRP projection of $5.40 on Sept. 21. That monthly chart accompanied his statement: “This is my long-term chart of $XRP. It implies an eventual advance to $5.40.” XRP traded near $1.54 then, making the projected level approximately 251% higher than the contemporaneous price.

His subsequent comments tied that interest to price history while challenging the unquestioning loyalty of some XRP supporters. In a Sept. 26 X post describing his chart-based reason to consider XRP, Brandt wrote: “The charts alone have always been enough reason for us to make a bet.” That assessment concerns his trading framework, distinct from the latest daily formation.

Institutional interest provides another perspective on XRP, with asset manager Bitwise’s investment chief emphasizing its history and familiar financial applications. Matt Hougan discussed XRP’s appeal to financial advisers in a video Token Relations shared Sept. 28. He pointed to cross-currency transfers and liquidity, the availability of assets needed to transact, as recognizable financial functions.

title: Ripple’s Schwartz Slams Fee Metric as 100x XRP Fee Hike Is Floated
summary: Blockchain fee revenue is a poor performance metric, according to Ripple’s David Schwartz. Responding to an XRP Ledger fee suggestion, he described transaction charges as friction the chain failed to remove and questioned whose interests the metric represents. Schwartz Questions Whose Interests High...
content:
Blockchain fee revenue is a poor performance metric, according to Ripple’s David Schwartz. Responding to an XRP Ledger fee suggestion, he described transaction charges as friction the chain failed to remove and questioned whose interests the metric represents.

Key Takeaways

  • Schwartz puts fee-paying users at the center of the blockchain debate.
  • An X user suggested a 10-fold or 100-fold base-fee increase.
  • Standard XRP Ledger transaction fees are destroyed, not paid to validators.

Schwartz Questions Whose Interests Higher Fees Serve

People paying to use a blockchain face costs that fee revenue metrics can overlook, according to David Schwartz, Ripple’s chief technology officer emeritus. In an exchange on X on Oct. 4, he criticized fee revenue as a metric and questioned whose interests it represents, responding to a suggestion that XRP Ledger validators raise transaction costs to burn more XRP.

Schwartz stated:

“I think fee revenue is a terrible metric since it measures how much friction the chain *didn’t* remove. If you represent the people who collect the fees, then fees are great. But what about the people who *pay* the fees? Who cares about their interests?”

His argument draws a distinction between income for fee recipients and the expense borne by people making transactions. On networks such as Bitcoin, cryptocurrency network fees compensate miners for including transactions. The response shifts attention from the amounts collected to the costs of using those systems.

XRP Fee Proposal Centers on Burns, Not Validator Income

The exchange began with an X user arguing that investors and analysts increasingly evaluate base-layer blockchains by fee revenue. These networks process transactions on their own ledgers. The user contended that XRPL’s fraction-of-a-cent charges make it look economically insignificant under that measure, even though inexpensive settlement is central to its purpose.

The user’s counterargument was that XRPL’s transaction fees are permanently destroyed rather than distributed to validators, the servers participating in consensus, or agreement on transactions. The user framed that supply reduction as a benefit for every XRP holder. In this view, higher charges would increase the amount burned per transaction rather than generate income for network operators.

A 10-fold or 100-fold increase in the base fee was suggested, with the claim that transactions could still cost well under one cent while burning more tokens. The dollar cost would depend on XRP’s price. XRP Ledger’s fee voting process allows trusted validators’ preferences to influence the base charge, with changes subject to consensus.

Such adjustments require collective agreement rather than a unilateral instruction from an executive or company. Schwartz previously described XRP Ledger’s design as limiting Ripple’s control. In February, he explained that the architecture deliberately restricted corporate authority. The fee proposal therefore concerns a decision by network participants rather than an increase Ripple could impose alone.

Larger XRP Burns Weighed Against Lower Transaction Costs

The X user asked whether larger burns justify higher costs or whether inexpensive payments and tokenization better support adoption. Tokenization means representing assets with blockchain-based tokens. Burning reduces supply without paying holders. Ripple describes XRP’s role in payments and liquidity, or the ability to trade without substantially moving prices, as practical uses of the asset.

Those applications also extend to assets other than XRP, including stablecoins, tokens designed to track currencies or other reference assets. Schwartz has described XRP Ledger’s expansion beyond payments. In June, he discussed enterprise uses and offerings such as tokenized stocks, funds, and loans. Low costs were central to the X user’s question about adoption.

The base charge also differs from expenses arising when a large trade moves market prices. In March, Schwartz discussed how XRP prices relate to payment efficiency, arguing that higher prices can make transfers cheaper, other things being equal. The documented minimum standard transaction fee is 10 drops, equivalent to 0.00001 XRP, with higher costs possible under load.

title: Plume Opens Onchain Door to Fidelity’s $28B Bond Giant
summary: Plume opened nBND on Oct. 5, giving investors blockchain-based exposure to Fidelity’s roughly $28 billion Total Bond ETF. But there’s a small catch. The exchange-traded fund (ETF) itself wasn’t tokenized, and its $28 billion hasn’t moved onchain. The nBND vehicle is a receipt token for a Nest vault ...
content:
Plume opened nBND on Oct. 5, giving investors blockchain-based exposure to Fidelity’s roughly $28 billion Total Bond ETF. But there’s a small catch. The exchange-traded fund (ETF) itself wasn’t tokenized, and its $28 billion hasn’t moved onchain. The nBND vehicle is a receipt token for a Nest vault holding FBND shares, and hours after launch, the new vault contained only about $48 in onchain assets.

Key Takeaways

  • Plume’s nBND opened Oct. 5 with Fidelity’s FBND as its primary reserve asset.
  • Fidelity’s roughly $28B FBND remains offchain while nBND wraps exposure to its shares.
  • Defillama recorded about $48 in nFBND assets shortly after Plume announced the vault.

A $28 Billion Bond Giant Gets a Blockchain Wrapper

A roughly $28 billion Fidelity bond ETF just acquired a blockchain doorway, but almost none of that mountain of money walked through it. Plume launched nBND on Oct. 5, offering onchain exposure to Fidelity Total Bond ETF (FBND), an actively managed fund spanning government, corporate, mortgage, high-yield, and emerging-market debt.

The wrinkle is considerable. Fidelity hasn’t tokenized FBND, and the fund’s billions remain firmly offchain. Instead, Plume’s Nest protocol wraps exposure to shares held inside a vault and issues investors a receipt token. Hours after the announcement, using the ticker nFBND, Defillama showed roughly $48 in onchain assets.

Plume Wants to Move Beyond Tokenized Treasury Bills

That tiny starting balance doesn’t make the structure trivial. Onchain fixed income has largely revolved around short-duration U.S. Treasuries and money-market-style products. Plume is betting institutional investors eventually want the rest of the bond counter, too.

“While the onchain fixed income market was originally concentrated in short-duration Treasuries and money market equivalents, these are the starting points, not the destination. Institutional allocators want duration, and active management, the same building blocks they use offchain,” Plume CEO and co-founder Chris Yin said on Monday.

FBND certainly brings duration. The traditional finance (TradFi) giant Fidelity launched the ETF in October 2014, and its own June figures put net assets at $26.6 billion. Third-party estimates around early October placed the fund near $28 billion. Fidelity’s quarterly review showed roughly six years of duration, a 4.74% 30-day SEC yield, and a portfolio weighted heavily toward investment-grade debt. In other words, Plume isn’t wrapping some crypto-native contraption. It’s plugging an old-fashioned bond portfolio into blockchain plumbing.

The $28 Billion Hasn’t Gone Anywhere

Here’s where the story gets its cold shower. nBND, also listed as nFBND, is a Nest vault receipt token. Investors depositing into the structure don’t become registered FBND shareholders, and Fidelity hasn’t hauled thousands of bond positions onto Plume Mainnet.

The roughly $28 billion figure belongs to FBND itself, not nBND. Early descriptions calling the product a “tokenized $28 billion ETF” blur a rather important line. Defillama classified nFBND as a wrapper and receipt token issued by Nest DAO LLC and recorded only about $48 in onchain assets shortly after launch.

The Experiment Starts at $48

The idea nevertheless goes further than another tokenized Treasury product. A receipt representing a diversified, actively managed bond ETF could theoretically become programmable collateral or move through decentralized finance (DeFi) applications without requiring the underlying securities to leave traditional custody.

Cynthia Lo Bessette, Fidelity Investments’ head of digital asset management, said Fidelity is working with Plume “to bring financial products on-chain,” pointing to programmable portfolios, collateral utility, and access to capital. Plume already has institutional names behind it, including Apollo Global Management, Galaxy, Brevan Howard, and Haun Ventures, while Nest operates Treasury and private-credit vaults.

Now comes the part that counts. A nearly $28 billion bond fund stands behind the product’s headline, but the blockchain experiment started with enough money to cover dinner. If serious allocators arrive, then the figures could change quickly. Until then, $48 tells the more interesting story.

Feature/Hero image source: X screenshot of Plume co-founder Teddy Pornprinya.

title: Brazil Calls Its Own Betting Laws Unconstitutional as Shutdown Begins
summary: Brazil’s government has asked the Supreme Court to strike down the core of the laws that created its licensed betting market, two years after defending them. The filing landed days before licensed sites go dark on Oct. 6, with Justice Luiz Fux yet to rule on industry requests to suspend the ban. Gov...
content:
Brazil’s government has asked the Supreme Court to strike down the core of the laws that created its licensed betting market, two years after defending them. The filing landed days before licensed sites go dark on Oct. 6, with Justice Luiz Fux yet to rule on industry requests to suspend the ban.

Key Takeaways

  • Brazil’s government lawyers asked the Supreme Court on Oct. 2 to void its 2018 and 2023 betting laws.
  • Licensed betting sites go dark Oct. 6 while Justice Luiz Fux weighs industry bids to suspend the ban.
  • Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro 82% odds against Lula in the Oct. 25 runoff after he led the first round.

Government Lawyers Say the ‘Dragon’ Was Untameable

The Attorney General’s Office (AGU), representing the federal government in court, filed its opinion on Oct. 2 in a 2024 challenge to the betting laws brought by the Prosecutor General’s Office, asking the court to strike down the 2018 law that legalized fixed-odds betting and most of the 2023 law that regulated it. In a separate 2024 case, the same office had called the framework constitutional, if at risk of becoming unconstitutional over time. The regulated market proved that “the ‘dragon’ was untameable,” the new opinion concludes.

The filing cites a roughly 140% rise in public health system visits recorded under gambling-disorder codes between January 2018 and December 2025, while acknowledging the figure does not count individual patients and cannot all be attributed to online sports betting. It also points to record household debt and to criminal factions using betting platforms to launder money.

The opinion follows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s Sept. 25 provisional measure banning online betting nine days before the election. Under the shutdown timeline, players have until 11:59 p.m. Brasília time on Oct. 5 to withdraw balances, after which the Finance Ministry has ordered licensed operators to redirect all traffic to a government page. The central bank has already barred Pix payments for fixed-odds betting, along with bank transfers and boletos. Crypto, which unlicensed sites commonly use, is outside those rules, the trade outlet BNLData noted.

The National Association of Games and Lotteries and the Brazilian Institute for Responsible Gaming asked Justice Fux to rule before the midnight cutoff, arguing that 83 companies paid 2.55 billion reais ($488 million) for five-year licenses that the measure extinguishes on Oct. 25 without refunds. Football club Flamengo, whose shirt sponsorship is worth roughly 268.5 million reais ($51 million) a season, filed its own urgent request, and at least 22 other clubs have gone to the court. On Oct. 2, Fux gave the government 72 hours to respond.

Lula heads into the presidential runoff behind Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who took just over 56 million votes in Sunday’s first round to Lula’s nearly 54 million, and the two meet again on Oct. 25, the day betting licenses expire. On Polymarket, Bolsonaro’s odds of winning the presidency stood at about 82% on Monday, in a market that has drawn more than $173 million in volume. The platform itself is blocked in Brazil.

Though Bolsonaro called Lula’s measure “populist, hypocritical, and electioneering,” he also said he backs a ban on online casino games but wants to keep sports betting legal.

title: Novig Says Trading Jumped 94% After Sydney Sweeney’s Viral Ad
summary: Sports-centric prediction market platform Novig says its trading volume nearly doubled around the launch of its Sydney Sweeney campaign, with first-time depositors more than tripling. The company-reported figures cover a window that also included the start of the NFL season, and a new funding round ...
content:
Sports-centric prediction market platform Novig says its trading volume nearly doubled around the launch of its Sydney Sweeney campaign, with first-time depositors more than tripling. The company-reported figures cover a window that also included the start of the NFL season, and a new funding round reportedly values Novig at $2 billion.

Key Takeaways

  • Novig says trading volume rose nearly 94% in the 20 days around its Sept. 9 Sydney Sweeney ad.
  • First-time depositors jumped more than 218% and app downloads climbed 187%, co-founder Jacob Fortinsky said.
  • The sports-only prediction market’s new funding round reportedly values it at $2 billion, up from $500 million.

The Figures Overlap With the NFL Kickoff

Novig co-founder Jacob Fortinsky shared the growth figures with CNBC, saying trading volume rose nearly 94% and first-time depositors more than 218% in the 20 days before and after the “Just Sports” campaign launched on Sept. 9. Active users climbed 96% month-over-month and 260% year-over-year in September, and app downloads rose more than 187%.

The numbers are Novig’s own, and the campaign landed alongside the start of the NFL season. Fortinsky said he had not expected the ad and the football kickoff together to bring in this much volume and this many first-time users. Before launching as a federally regulated prediction market on Aug. 4, Novig ran a sweepstakes product using virtual currencies, so the year-over-year comparison spans that switch.

In the viral ad, Sweeney appears nude behind footballs, basketballs, and hockey gear, and tells viewers the platform offers “no betting on wars or deaths, and no politics.” She joined Novig as an equity holder after approaching the company, according to Fortinsky, though Novig has not disclosed the size of her stake. The campaign drew criticism from some female athletes, who said it set back how women in sports are perceived.

“Ultimately, I think we have nothing to apologize for and are very proud of the work that we did,” Fortinsky said, adding that he respected the opinions raised and that the team is a fan of women’s sports.

Third-party data points the same way, though Novig remains a small player. According to Aldrin Research data, the company’s sports volume grew 136% between the 30 days to Aug. 30 and the 30 days to Sept. 29, lifting its share of a market that reached $68.2 billion in sports and combo volume from 1.5% to 2%. Kalshi’s share was 73.4%.

Novig only admits users aged 21 and over, while Kalshi and Polymarket U.S. allow 18-year-olds, and it has sued several states over their authority to regulate its sports contracts. Fortinsky tied those choices to the company’s culture, saying, “We have to be willing to take outsized risk relative to the size of the company, doing that in a responsible way, of course.”

Novig has raised new funding at a $2 billion valuation, The Wall Street Journal reported last week, citing people familiar with the matter; Front Office Sports reported the same day that the round was still in progress, with Novig confirming that it is fundraising.

The reported valuation is four times the $500 million Novig reached when it closed a $75 million Series B in February, led by Pantera Capital. Novig did not say how much it is raising or which investors are involved.

title: Crypto PAC announces support for 32 House candidates in US midterms
summary: Fairshake said it would financially back 32 House candidates who all voted in favor of the CLARITY market structure bill in 2025, as the legislation remains in limbo in the Senate.
content:
Fairshake, the political action committee (PAC) backed by contributions from Coinbase, Ripple Labs and Andreessen Horowitz, announced that it would initially spend a combined $6 million on six House of Representatives candidates out of 32 people the group planned to back ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections.

On Monday, Fairshake said that it would support 19 Republican and 13 Democratic incumbents in US House races for 2026. The PAC is expected to spend more than $100 million on ads supporting House and Senate candidates in 2026, including at least $30 million in Ohio’s Senate race to back Republican Jon Husted over Democrat Sherrod Brown. 

“Fairshake has always been and always will be an issue-focused organization,” said Fairshake spokesperson Geoff Vetter. “We back pro-crypto candidates who support American innovation in both parties.”

According to the crypto-backed PAC, three Republican and three Democratic candidates will each receive $1 million in spending ahead of the 2026 midterms. These politicians included Oregon Representative Janelle Bynum, California Representative Derek Tran and Nevada Representative Steven Horsford on the Democratic side and Arkansas Representative French Hill, Michigan Representative Bill Huizenga and Wisconsin Representative Bryan Steil as Republicans.

All 32 candidates Fairshake said would receive its support voted to advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, a bill that had been expected to establish clear roles for US financial agencies in overseeing digital assets. The legislation failed to pass a crucial Senate vote, leaving the Republican-led bill’s future uncertain ahead of the midterm elections. Many polls showed Democrats favored to take majority control of both the House and Senate in 2027.

Vetter said in August that Fairshake had “$122 million cash on hand” ahead of the midterms as part of its plan to “help build the largest pro-crypto caucus in American history.” The consumer advocacy group Public Citizen reported that the PAC had spent $82 million on ads opposing or backing candidates as of June, less than half of the $189 million it estimated came from advocacy groups and companies aligned with the crypto industry.

Related: CLARITY vote failure could stoke more crypto PAC spending in key races

title: FinCEN withdraws proposed crypto mixing rule over ‘legitimate activity’ concerns
summary: The bureau under the US Treasury said it was withdrawing two proposed rules on unhosted wallets and crypto mixers ”as part of the Trump Administration’s deregulatory agenda.”
content:
The US Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) withdrew two proposed rules affecting its enforcement of crypto companies, including one on “convertible virtual currency mixing.” 

According to a Monday notice, the agency will withdraw a December 2020 proposal that would have imposed “recordkeeping, verification, and reporting requirements” related to crypto transactions and unhosted wallets, as well as one affecting enforcement of crypto mixing services. FinCEN said that the mixer rule, initially proposed in October 2023, “could have a chilling effect on legitimate activity and place a large reporting burden on covered financial institutions.”

“FinCEN has considered the comments submitted in response to these proposals and is withdrawing them as part of the Trump Administration’s deregulatory agenda and ongoing efforts to ensure digital asset regulations are fit-for-purpose,” the Monday notice said.

The US agency’s regulatory action is the latest in a series of moves by departments tasked with overseeing crypto assets, citing the Trump administration’s crypto agenda. Earlier today, Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chair Michael Selig announced that the agency was using its “existing statutory authorities“ to propose two rules on how crypto companies could operate under its purview without additional authority from Congress.

Many advocacy groups for the crypto and blockchain industry lauded FinCEN for reversing course on crypto mixers and reporting requirements related to unhosted wallets. In a Monday X post, the Crypto Council for Innovation called the move “positive for the digital asset ecosystem.”

title: Binance Launches Retail AI Assistant, Repackages Existing Trading Tools
summary:
Binance has grouped its artificial intelligence products under a new Binance Intelligence brand, combining a newly launched retail market assistant with two trading tools that were already available in some form. 
Binance AI began rolling out to eligible users in New Zealand on 5 October and is expe...
content:
2026-10-05T22:40:00.000+02:00

Monday, 05/10/2026 | 20:40 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Binance has grouped its AI products under the new Binance Intelligence brand, but only its retail market assistant represents a clearly new live rollout.
  • Binance has not explained how the upcoming AI Pro release will differ from the paid beta available since March.

Binance has grouped its artificial intelligence products under a new Binance Intelligence brand, combining a newly launched retail market assistant with two trading tools that were already available in some form.

Binance AI began rolling out to eligible users in New Zealand on 5 October and is expected to reach additional markets over the coming days. Agent OS has operated since August, while a limited paid beta of Binance AI Pro has been available since March.

AI Pro Was Already Available as a Paid Beta

Binance says AI Pro will launch in the coming weeks, although the exchange introduced a limited beta on 25 March. The beta cost $9.99 per month after a seven-day trial, with Binance listing a regular monthly price of $29.99.

It allowed users to connect AI models to a dedicated sub-account and automate spot and perpetual orders, leveraged borrowing, market monitoring and custom trading strategies.

The AI account was separated from the customer’s main account, and its API key could not withdraw or transfer funds. Users had to move capital into the sub-account before the agent could execute trades.

The latest version is presented as a no-code workflow builder. Users will be able to describe a strategy in plain language, test it through paper trading and activate it for live execution after reviewing the resulting workflow. Trading will remain subject to the permissions, and limits chosen by the user.

Binance has not explained whether the forthcoming release will replace the existing beta, extend it to more users or introduce a different pricing model.

Paper trading was not listed among the functions in the March beta announcement, suggesting that the product has changed since its initial release.

Binance AI Begins Retail Rollout

The clearly new live product is Binance AI, an assistant integrated into the exchange’s app. It provides market briefings, profit-and-loss summaries, price alerts and information on sentiment, macroeconomic developments and activity across crypto sectors.

Where personalisation is enabled, the assistant can adapt the information displayed using a client’s holdings, preferences and previous product usage. Its announced functions centre on research and portfolio monitoring rather than automated execution.

The service is free. Binance launched it first for eligible users in New Zealand and said a wider rollout would follow, although availability will remain subject to regional eligibility.

Agent OS Remains the Developer Tool

The third component, Agent OS, was launched in August for developers and technically experienced users building external AI agents. It connects those applications to Binance functions including market data, trading, wallets, payments and on-chain services.

Agents operate through dedicated sub-accounts with permissions set by the user. Withdrawals are prohibited, access can be revoked and an emergency control can disconnect connected agents.

As Finance Magnates previously reported, Binance supplies the account connections, execution infrastructure and controls, while the external developer remains responsible for the agent itself.

Binance Intelligence gives these products a common name and divides them among developers, app users and traders seeking no-code automation.

Their availability remains fragmented, however: the retail assistant is beginning its geographic rollout, Agent OS is already operational, and the next stage of AI Pro has yet to be distinguished clearly from its existing paid beta.

title: Modern Treasury seeks US trust bank charter for digital asset custody
summary: The payments infrastructure company is seeking federal approval to offer stablecoin custody and related fiat services through a limited-purpose national trust bank.
content:
Payments infrastructure company Modern Treasury has applied to establish a US national trust bank that would provide digital asset custody and related fiat services.

According to Monday’s announcement, the company submitted an application to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to establish Modern Treasury National Trust Bank, which would operate as a federally regulated, limited-purpose national trust bank.

If approved, the bank would allow Modern Treasury customers to custody and move stablecoins and fiat through an integrated service, but would not issue stablecoins or make loans.

“We believe stablecoins are foundational economic infrastructure for the future,” Modern Treasury co-founder and CEO Matt Marcus said, adding that the company has fully integrated stablecoins into its payments platform.

Modern Treasury said the proposed bank would operate separately from its existing payments business, which has facilitated more than $600 billion in payments across hundreds of organizations.

The application comes amid a broader push by crypto and payments companies for national trust bank charters. Bastion and Ripple have received conditional approvals, while Circle and BitGo have received final approvals. Kraken parent Payward, Zerohash and Block have also submitted applications.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, the CFTC moved ahead with its own crypto regulatory framework after the CLARITY Act stalled in the Senate, Metaplanet unveiled a new income strategy to support further Bitcoin accumulation and an OKX joint venture with NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange filed to launch a 24/7 tokenized US stock trading platform.

CFTC moves ahead on crypto rules after CLARITY stalls

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) is moving ahead with a new crypto regulatory framework after the Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act, with Chair Michael Selig saying the agency will use its existing authority to act without Congress.

The CFTC issued an advance notice of proposed rulemaking covering platforms that allow retail customers to trade crypto using margin, leverage or financing. Under the proposal, the agency would create a new category of designated contract market called a “crypto asset market,” or CAM, giving qualifying exchanges a path to operate under uniform federal oversight rather than a patchwork of state rules.

The framework would not cover ordinary spot crypto exchanges, which generally remain subject to state money-transmission laws, although the CFTC retains authority over fraud and market manipulation.

The move follows the Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) own proposal for a tailored crypto securities regime and signals that both agencies are prepared to pursue new rules despite the CLARITY Act’s failure in the Senate.

Their efforts are advancing with unusually thin leadership. Hester Peirce’s departure leaves the SEC with two commissioners, while Selig remains the CFTC’s sole commissioner and chair.

Metaplanet reveals net income strategy to fuel Bitcoin accumulation

Japanese investment and Bitcoin treasury company Metaplanet introduced a net interest income strategy on Monday, seeking to invest capital in income-generating assets and use the net interest to fuel its Bitcoin accumulation and dividend payments.

The move is part of the company’s revised capital allocation policy under which 10% to 15% of assets can move into strategic investments, including mergers and acquisitions and interest-generating assets.

Bitcoin (BTC) remains the company’s core treasury reserve asset, accounting for 85% to 90% of total assets, Metaplanet revealed in a Monday notice. The decision aims to enhance the Japanese company’s financing capacity and credit quality to grow its BTC holdings per share through additional acquisitions.

The company revealed the fundraising model in the wake of shareholder concerns about Metaplanet’s governance and complex capital structure. On Friday, Metaplanet issued five corrected securities filings clarifying that CEO Simon Gerovich does not hold majority voting rights in MMX Ventures, a shareholder in Metaplanet.

OKX, NYSE parent file to launch tokenized US stock platform

An OKX joint venture has filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission to launch a tokenized stock trading platform.

OKXICE LLC, a joint venture between cryptocurrency exchange operator OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange Inc., has notified the SEC that it intends to launch a tokenized securities venue (TSV) under the SEC’s new innovation exemption.

The platform will include more than 60 companies listed on US stock exchanges, said OKXICE co-chair Andrew Cuomo.

“The digital asset revolution is already transforming our financial system. Tokenized securities are part of what comes next,” he added. 

A public notice dated Oct. 4 lists 63 proposed stock symbols, including Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft and Tesla, alongside crypto companies such as Strategy, Coinbase, Circle and Bitgo. 

The OKXICE platform plans to operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, using permissioned Uniswap v4 liquidity pools deployed on XLayer. Each tokenized stock would be paired with USDC (USDC), Global Dollar (USDG) or USDt (USDT).

title: Crypto's campaign arm, Fairshake, sets lists of U.S. House favorites it'll spend on
summary: The super PAC shared a list of more than 30 incumbent candidates it's backing, with about a million dollars going to three names from each party.
content:
Oct 5, 2026, 3:21 p.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Fairshake, the crypto super PAC, said it's supporting 32 House incumbents in their November elections, divided between the parties.
  • The pro-crypto candidates are in generally safe seats, which could help the industry in its relationships with well-placed lawmakers.

The crypto industry's leading political action committee, Fairshake, released another list of candidates it's supporting for the November elections, backing 13 Democrats and 19 Republicans — all incumbents — in their U.S. House of Representatives races.

The candidates tend to be safe bets to return to Congress, potentially further reinforcing the existing support for crypto policies in Congress. Atop all those names, six of them are getting a million dollars each in support from Fairshake and its affiliates, according to a spokesman for the super PAC.

“Fairshake has always been and always will be an issue-focused organization," said Spokesman Geoff Vetter in a statement. "We back pro-crypto candidates who support American innovation in both parties."

The top recipients on the Republican side are three well-known names in crypto circles, including French Hill, the chairman of the House Financial Services Committee who led the charge for crypto legislation in the House; Bill Huizenga, a senior member of that committee, and Bryan Steil, another member who also leads the subcommittee on digital assets.

For Democrats, the higher support level is going to Steven Horsford, a Nevada lawmaker who helped get a bipartisan crypto tax bill through the House tax committee he serves on, and Derek Tran of California, Fairshake said. Both of them have an "A" rating on digital assets issues from Stand With Crypto, as does the third recipient, Janelle Bynum.

Bynum is an Oregon Democrat incumbent who had beaten Republican Lori Chavez-DeRemer for her seat two years ago. Chavez-DeRemer, who was backed by Fairshake in the prior election, went on to run President Donald Trump's Department of Labor, though she resigned earlier this year under multiple misconduct allegations. Bynum voted for crypto bills during her first term and appeared at the Digital Chamber's DC Blockchain Summit earlier this year.

The 32 House incumbents on Fairshake's latest list are well targeted for the industry's next legislative maneuvers, with many of them on the House Ways and Means Committee that will deal with crypto tax issues, and many others on the key House Financial Services Committee. Agriculture, science and judiciary panels — each promising to be important for future crypto bills — also are represented by the candidates.

Vetter said his organization has so far backed 53 winners out of 57 races in the primaries and is working toward "the largest pro-crypto caucus in American history." In many of those primaries, Fairshake favored a candidate from the party that's likely to win the general election — a strategy it succeeded with in the prior election.

The House hasn't been the source of the industry's greatest legislative difficulty, though. Though the U.S. Senate did approve a major crypto bill, the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act (GENIUS) Act last year, things didn't go as well in the Senate for the more important market structure bill sought in recent months.

Despite the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act crashing last month, Fairshake hasn't embarked on a public campaign to unseat senators who voted against the bill, which included all Democrats and a few Republicans. The PAC's biggest opposition campaign is targeting former Senator Sherood Brown, the Ohio Democrat who once ran a crypto-resistant Senate Banking Committee and is trying to return to the Senate. Fairshake has devoted some $30 million to defeat him, and a PAC established by Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss has thrown in another $3 million against Brown.

Fairshake's spending has been devoted to independent buys of advertising, outside of the campaigns' involvement. The super PAC doesn't mention crypto as an issue in those ads, instead focusing on the topics it determines have the best chance of swaying voters.

title: Advocacy group pushes back on banks’ lawsuit against OCC over charters
summary: CCI CEO Ji Hun Kim said that the organization “remains confident“ in the OCC’s approval of charters for crypto companies, despite a recent lawsuit and pushback from some lawmakers.
content:
The Crypto Council for Innovation (CCI) has backed the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency’s (OCC’s) move to approve several charters for crypto companies, saying a lawsuit filed by the Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA) was an attempt to stifle innovation. 

On Monday, CCI CEO Ji Hun Kim said that the ICBA lawsuit was a “clear attempt to resist national trust charters, payments innovation, and competition in financial services.” The crypto advocacy organization supported the OCC’s approvals and conditional approvals of crypto companies for national trust charters, despite accusations from some lawmakers that exchanges “want to evade the fundamental safeguards and obligations that come with being a bank.”

The ICBA legal action, filed on Friday in the US District ​Court for the District of Columbia, alleged that the OCC approved US bank charters for entities, including crypto companies, without sufficient safeguards or compliance with requirements normally used for banks.

“Congress did not create the national trust charter as a side door into the banking system for crypto firms seeking the credibility of a federal bank charter without the Community Reinvestment Act obligations, consolidated supervision, capital and liquidity standards, and FDIC insurance that apply to insured depository institutions,” said ICBA president and CEO Rebeca Romero Rainey in a Friday statement.

Among the applications the OCC has approved or conditionally approved under US President Donald Trump were those from World Liberty Financial, Circle, Ripple, Fidelity Digital Assets, BitGo and Paxos. 

Many lawmakers criticized the World Liberty approval, which came under the leadership of OCC head Jonathan Gould, a Trump pick who has served since July 2025. Members of the Trump family co-founded the crypto company, which has been the target of probes over alleged ties to the royal families of the United Arab Emirates.

title: AvaTrade Picks Brokerage and Trading Infrastructure Veteran as CFO
summary:
Jeremy Schlachter has joined AvaTrade as Chief Financial Officer after leaving the same position at The NAGA Group in August, bringing experience across retail brokerage, B2B trading infrastructure and corporate transformation. 
Schlachter announced the move in a LinkedIn post on Sunday, saying he w...
content:
2026-10-05T21:06:16.270+02:00

Monday, 05/10/2026 | 19:06 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Jeremy Schlachter joins AvaTrade after serving as CFO of NAGA.
  • He succeeds Sari Hemmendinger, who spent about 11 years at AvaTrade.

Jeremy Schlachter has joined AvaTrade as Chief Financial Officer after leaving the same position at The NAGA Group in August, bringing experience across retail brokerage, B2B trading infrastructure and corporate transformation.

Schlachter announced the move in a LinkedIn post on Sunday, saying he would work with the team to support AvaTrade’s “continued growth and ambitions.”

Experience Spans Brokerage and B2B Infrastructure

Schlachter joined NAGA’s management team in 2025 and served as CFO during the listed fintech group’s integration of CAPEX.com and efforts to reduce operating costs.

Before NAGA, he was Group CFO of Finalto, the B2B liquidity and trading technology provider previously owned by Playtech. He had earlier served as Vice President of Finance at Playtech and later as CFO of gaming technology company Skywind Group.

His background gives AvaTrade a finance executive familiar with the economics of retail brokerage, institutional trading infrastructure and businesses undergoing corporate transformation.

Schlachter succeeds Sari Hemmendinger, who spent about 11 years at AvaTrade. According to her LinkedIn profile, she joined the broker as Vice President of Finance before becoming Group CFO.

AvaTrade Considers Acquisition and Reshapes European Footprint

The appointment comes as AvaTrade considers expansion through a potential acquisition while adjusting parts of its European operations.

In June, Finance Magnates reported that AvaTrade had submitted an offer to acquire Stratos, the Jefferies-owned operator of the FXCM and Tradu brands. A cryptocurrency exchange had reportedly submitted a competing bid. No transaction has been announced.

More recently, AvaTrade decided to close its Polish branch almost six years after opening the local office. Polish clients and partners are expected to remain supported through the broker’s international operations.

AvaTrade has not identified Schlachter’s immediate priorities. His appointment nevertheless brings experience in acquisitions, business integration and trading infrastructure to the finance function as the broker weighs its next phase of expansion.

summary: Geneva, Switzerland — October 5, 2026 — The Office of Justin Sun today announced the newest recipients of the Justin Sun Prize: independent researcher Wouter van Doorn, mathematics Ph.D. student Quanyu Tang, and mathematics researcher Yanyang Li from Nanjing’s Southeast University, recognized for co...
